title: Patient-Weighted While-Alive Effects under Early Death and Infinite-Variance Scores
banked_reason: D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4; graded tier field capped at subfield because the one-recurrence known-mechanism theory lacks fitted-estimator transport and implementation-level demonstration.
gap_reasons: It does not prove analogous behavior for the fitted mets::WA_recurrent estimator, unknown censoring or intensity envelopes, multiple recurrences, or fixed-grid recorded data, so its practical reach is materially narrower than the motivating clinical workflow.

The projected paper score is limited by the specialized one-recurrence model, strong known-mechanism requirements for uniform inference, and the absence of an implementation-level or empirical demonstration connecting the theory to the published estimator.

proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived the exact index-two tail coefficient and second-moment boundary, joint limit and empirical studentization, and a complete-history minimax risk order with a matching known-envelope honest interval. The derivation also established a denominator-floor time-resolution frontier for an explicit constructed score, while leaving transport to the fitted mets::WA_recurrent output open. D0.5 math and rubric checks passed, but the general referee capped the delivered package at subfield because the scope and implementation link did not meet the field paper-score floor.
tldr: The identity patient-weighted while-alive effect is point identified in a randomized illness--death study, yet recurrence followed by death arbitrarily close to enrollment places its observable score exactly at the infinite-variance Gaussian boundary. The project derives the \(r_{a0}d_{1a0}/2\) tail coefficient, the exact second-moment criterion, and a feasible \(\sqrt{n/\log n}\) joint limit. Its main contribution is a complete-history minimax theorem: over bounded intensities with a known envelope, squared risk is of order \(\log(n)/n\), and an explicit clipped estimator supports a finite-sample honest interval of matching length. Transport to the fitted \(\texttt{mets::WA\_recurrent}\) procedure remains an explicit open question.
gap: Published while-alive work derives exposure-weighted and composite estimand values under shared gamma frailty, conditional targeting properties for quasi-Poisson and LWYY procedures, and regular Gaussian theory for a fitted identity-PWWA estimator, but it does not locate the continuous-time positive-origin moment boundary or establish precision limits for estimators that use the full recurrence and death histories.
fill: The project derives the exact tail and joint studentized limit, constructs a bounded legal hazard perturbation for the complete-history minimax converse, and matches it with a clipped estimator and a uniformly honest known-envelope interval.
